chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked (makruh) that there be in the house of the Muslim man a dog.

key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: The dog - the specific animal discussed in the ruling.
key_terms.دَارِ: House or residence - referring to the domestic dwelling.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a category of legal ruling indicating it is recommended to avoid but not strictly forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping a dog inside a Muslim's house?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the dislike (makruh) of keeping dogs within the home, a ruling often contextualized by scholars as relating to the preservation of ritual purity and the spiritual atmosphere of the household. While general utility dogs are permitted, this specific narration emphasizes the preference for excluding them from living quarters to maintain domestic sanctity, a view supported by the broader Shia jurisprudential tradition.
